sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area/Volume
lecture_lines: The determinant is the signed area of a parallelogram.
Vectors form the sides of this geometric shape.
Area scaling helps us understand linear transformations.
animations: Fade in two basis vectors v1=(2,0) and v2=(0,3).
Draw parallelogram spanned by v1 and v2, filled with color #444444.

sections.title: Framing the Linear System
lecture_lines: We represent Ax=b as a vector equation.
Scales x and y reach a target point b.
Think of reaching a crumb using two paths.
animations: Show vector A=(1,2) and vector B=(3,1) starting at origin.
Display target point b=(5,5) on the plane.
Animate dashed lines showing x*A + y*B = b.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution
lecture_lines: Replace a column with the target vector b.
New parallelograms emerge from this replacement.
Area ratios reveal the needed scale factors.
The ratio gives x for the first column.
This process defines Cramer's elegant rule.
animations: Display the original parallelogram formed by A and B.
Swap column A with vector b to form a new parallelogram.

sections.title: Visualization of the Solution
lecture_lines: Visualize the parallelogram area changing dynamically.
The expansion factor directly represents coordinate x.
This visually confirms the determinant ratio identity.
Shrinking areas show lower coordinate values.
Expanding areas show higher coordinate values.
animations: Show the area of the Ax parallelogram as it scales.
Overlay the ratio formula: 'x = Det(Ax) / Det(A)'.
Flash the resulting scalar value x to highlight the solution.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: Cramer's Rule is a geometric ratio of space.
Flat space prevents reaching the target point.
animations: Display a 2D plane with two collinear vectors forming a flat shape.
Show the determinant text 'Det(A) = 0' flashing in red.
Show the target b off-line and display 'No Solution' text.
